A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MGSV task, MGSV-EC dataset and MaDe method. All supplied pages, including figures, tables, equations and end matter, support comparison. Neither PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results, component ablations, inference measurements and a human evaluation on 100 test videos in Section 5.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical evaluations and adds results across random data splits and training-data sizes, alongside a revised human evaluation.

M1.justification: MaDe's architecture, losses and inference procedure in Section 4 remain unchanged, including X-Pool matching and the single-query, six-CA decoder. The added concatenation explanation describes an operation already present in v2's Equation 4.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same MGSV-EC corpus of 53,194 videos and 4,050 music tracks using SmG, V2MR and MsG. Additional splits and training subsets retain the same coverage. The human evaluation retains the same stated participant population.

E2.justification: Table 4 retains the same eight grounding baselines, MVPt/MVPt+, MVPt+ / UVCOM+ and CONQUER. The human comparison also retains MVPt+ / UVCOM+. New split and training-size analyses reuse existing comparators.

E3.justification: v3 adds two random splits following the existing partition protocol and a training-size sweep from 20% to 100%. The reported human panel changes from 10 participants (7 male, 3 female) to 20 (15 male, 5 female), retaining 100 test videos and the same response options. Main metrics and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Table 5 tests robustness across data splits for MaDe and MVPt+ / UVCOM+. New Figure 5 examines training-size sensitivity for MaDe, QD-DETR, UVCOM and their fusion-without-CA variants. Existing component ablations, decoder-depth tests and efficiency analysis are retained.

E5.justification: v3 supplements single-split method scores with averages and ± quantities across three splits in Table 5, explicitly reporting two additional random-split experiments. The meaning of ± is not defined, and no explicit confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure is added.

E6.justification: Table 4 and existing ablation and efficiency values remain unchanged. New Table 5 reports mIoU 0.743±0.017 for MaDe versus 0.676±0.013 for MVPt+ / UVCOM+, and Figure 5 adds scaling results. Human preferences change from 39.4% versus 28.0% to 38.1% versus 28.6% under the larger reported panel; these are revised evaluation results, not a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 and the mathematical descriptions of matching and detection losses are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusions retain the same central claims: introducing MGSV and MGSV-EC and establishing MaDe as a strong unified baseline. Added robustness evidence supports these existing claims without redefining the central contributions.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly discusses subjective music selection, practitioner comparability and diversity, and adds personalization as an unresolved limitation. Section 5.3 interprets the new training-size trends as evidence of CA fusion's incompatibility with MGSV, while retaining the unresolved question about its fundamental mechanism.

D1.justification: v3 adds a concrete project repository link on the first page and removes the abstract's future release promise; the PDFs alone do not establish repository contents or availability. Implementation settings remain unchanged. Figure 2 drops the explicit statement that video tags are not used for modeling.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 34 works and retain the same positioning relative to video grounding, video corpus moment retrieval and video-to-music retrieval. Acronym expansion and equivalent decoder notation do not change that positioning.

P1.justification: v3 corrects grammar and some table references, expands terminology, clarifies concatenation, updates author ordering and notes, and adds brief framing and acknowledgments. The section organization and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 5 and Figure 5, redraws the human-evaluation pie chart, and revises Figure 1's illustrative durations and moment boundaries. Table 4 becomes a smaller single-column display; existing ablation, decoder-depth and efficiency tables are relocated or renumbered, with some shortened captions.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's single-split evidence, the added split and training-size analyses provide modestly stronger support for the retained conclusions. The larger reported human panel and explicit discussion of subjectivity and personalization also help. These gains outweigh limited presentation drawbacks: the new ± quantities remain undefined, and compressed results tables are harder to read.
